# TME clustering

`tme_cluster` is not executed by `runall`. This chapter clusters samples using the CIBERSORT fractions that `runall` already produced.

## Inspect the input

```bash
head results/gbm-demo/05-tme/cibersort_results.csv
iobrpy-cli tme_cluster --help
```

The input is a sample-by-feature table. The first column is treated as the sample ID, and `--features 1:22` selects the 22 CIBERSORT cell-fraction columns after that ID column.

## Run the teaching example

There are only four samples, so restrict the candidate cluster range:

```bash
mkdir -p results/gbm-demo/09-tme-cluster

iobrpy-cli tme_cluster \
  --input results/gbm-demo/05-tme/cibersort_results.csv \
  --output results/gbm-demo/09-tme-cluster/tme_clusters.csv \
  --features 1:22 \
  --min_nc 2 \
  --max_nc 3 \
  --print_result
```

The output contains the sample ID, a label such as `TME1`, and the selected scaled features:

```bash
column -s, -t < results/gbm-demo/09-tme-cluster/tme_clusters.csv | head
```

Four samples are enough to demonstrate the command but not to establish reproducible molecular subtypes. A research cohort needs enough samples to support the requested cluster range, stability analysis, and external validation.
